Summary
A new edition of this best-selling history of Britain, from Roman times, now updated to cover the first decade of the 21st century. The Oxford History of Britain tells the story of Britain and its people over two thousand years, from the coming of the Roman legions to the present day.

Highlights of the British Collection:

The End of Roman Oxfordshire

The Romans withdrew formal administration and military forces from Britain in about AD 410. There has been much debate about what happened next: continuity and/or Dark Age chaos?
New techniques and new legislation in archaeology can help our understanding of this difficult, transitional period of history.

Overall, probably the most significant factor in economic and social change was the gradual abandonment of coinage: from the final years of the fourth century AD, Britain became demonetised.

Peter Salway (født 1932 ) er en britisk historiker , spesialist på romersk Britannia . Han var forleser for Open University og ble senere medlem ( fellow ) av fakultet Sidney Sussex College ved University of Cambridge , og deretter ved All Souls College ved University of Oxford . [ 3 ] Han er nå pensjonist, men fortsatt tilknyttet Oxford som professor emeritus . Det historieverk som Salway er mest kjent for er The Oxford Illustrated History of Roman Britain , 1993 .
